messages.author: 893322b7081eeb7e
messages.subject: Trouble running a multisession model
parts:
I am attempting to run a multisession model for a rabbit population with 2 sessions and 2 occasions per session (population was surveyed twice in 2018 and twice in 2019). My input is a capt file that includes data from both years, a list of trap files (one for each year), and a list of masks (one for each year, because I am running this for a metapopulation, and some sites were not surveyed in both years so the masks differ slightly by year). 

First I tried the following code, but the output for session 1 and session 2 was exactly the same, when I was expecting different estimates by year:

captures1819<- read.table("capeelizCapt.txt")

#create trapfile
trapfile18<- read.traps("capeeliz_proxtrap_18.txt", detector = "proximity")
trapfile19<- read.traps("capeeliz_proxtrap_19.txt", detector = "proximity")
trapfile<-list(trapfile18,trapfile19)

#2018mask
mask1<- read.mask(file = "capeeliz18_mask.txt", spacing = 30)
#2019mask
mask2<- read.mask(file = "capeeliz19_mask.txt", spacing = 30)
#metapop1819mask
mask <-list(mask1,mask2)

CHmetapop <-make.capthist(captures1819, trapfile, 
                          fmt = "XY", noccasions = 2, tol = 3, snapXY = TRUE)

summary(CHmetapop, terse=TRUE)
verify(CHmetapop, report = 2)

metapop.fit <- secr.fit (CHmetapop, model = list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~1), CL = FALSE, detectfn = 0, method = "Newton-Raphson", mask=mask)

metapop.fit


Then I tried the same code, but made a change to the secr.fit argument following p. 6 of secr-multisession.pdf, with the following change to the code starting on the secr.fit line:

library(MASS)
metapop.fit <- secr.fit (CHmetapop, model = D~session, CL = FALSE, detectfn = 0, method = "Newton-Raphson", mask=mask, details=list(contrasts=list(session=MASS::contr.sdif)))

coef(metapop.fit)

beta <- coef(metapop.fit)[2:3, 'beta']
sebeta <- coef(metapop.fit)[2:3, 'SE.beta']
exp(beta)

exp(beta)*sqrt(exp(sebeta^2)-1)
D<-collate(metapop.fit, realnames='D')[,1,1,]
D[2:3]/D[1:2]


I got the error on the collate step "Warning message:
In collate(metapop.fit, realnames = "D") : only one model"

So it seems I am having an issue getting secr to recognize that I want estimates for each year separately, and also for the two years combined. Any suggestions on achieving both yearly estimates and a combined estimate for the two years would be greatly appreciated.

Best,
Melissa

messages.subject: Re: Trouble running a multisession model
parts:
I would have thought predict(metapop.fit) gives you session-specific densities from the second fit, and predict(metapop.fit) from the first fit will give you an overall density (or back-transform the relevant coefficient from the second fit). What am I missing? Collate is literally for collating predictions from different models in a single table.
.

parts: Thanks for the quick response and sorry for the confusion. Maybe I am just missing something, I've read the user guides and am still not understanding the approach to take for getting an overall density (both years combined) plus yearly densities. I can do the yearly densities as single sessions, so I'm more interested in getting an overall density that takes into consideration that data is coming from 2 years (rather than running the two years as a single session, i.e. 4 occasions, 2 per year). I just did the predict(metapop.fit) and this is what I got for output (screenshot attached). This is the code I used:
metapop.fit <- secr.fit (CHmetapop, model = list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~1), CL = FALSE, detectfn = 0, method = "Newton-Raphson", mask=mask)

predict(metapop.fit)


I'm not understanding why it gives me the same results for the two sessions (i.e. the two years) and which one would be considered the overall estimate with the two years combined. My apologies if this is something simple and I'm just not understanding.

messages.subject: Re: Trouble running a multisession model
parts: You fitted two different models with the name metapop.fit (perhaps confusing yourself) - one with D~1 (density constant across sessions) and one with D~session (density differs between sessions). Results from predict() will differ accordingly.
